title: Sandalwood and castor
hookLine: You are sandalwood and I the poor castor plant beside You, made fragrant by Your nearness (Asa, Ravidas, ang 486)

cards: Sandalwood is prized for its scent, and its fragrance can linger on whatever it touches. The castor plant is a scrappy, weedy shrub that springs up along roadsides and in waste ground.

Nobody plants a castor bush for its smell. Ravidas, who sang a whole city without sorrow, turns now to himself, and reaches for these two plants. He sets them side by side in a hymn, and he knows exactly which one he is.

teach.h: YOU ARE SANDALWOOD, I THE CASTOR.
teach.b: The hymn is in Raag Asa, on Ang 486. In paraphrase, Ravidas sings to the Lord: You are sandalwood, and I am the poor castor plant, living close beside You.

From a lowly tree I've become a lofty one, for Your sweet fragrance has come to dwell in me. Hear how the change happens. The castor doesn't turn into sandalwood, or train or strive its way to a better scent.
It grows near, and the fragrance moves across the gap and settles in.
Nearness does the work. Ravidas keeps going with more pairs.

teach.h: SILK AND A WORM; THE HOLY COMPANY.
teach.b: In paraphrase: You are silk, white and yellow, and I am a poor worm. Then the refrain: Madho, I seek the shelter of the company of Your holy ones; I'm full of faults, and You are generous.
The company of the holy ones, in Sikh words sangat, is where the nearness happens.

teach.h: NOT BY CHANGING, BUT BY STANDING NEAR.
teach.b: It's not only the Lord far above. It's the people you stand beside. A gathering where the Name is sung can rub off on whoever sits in it.
And this is the leather-worker from two days ago, whose people some refused to touch.
He doesn't deny that he feels low. He says it plainly. But he doesn't stay there.
A low plant beside sandalwood comes away smelling of something else, not by changing what it is, but by where it chose to stand.

how: Ravidas's sandalwood hymn is sung in kirtan as gurbani, and Sikhs often use its picture to speak of the sangat, the holy company, whose nearness shapes the one who joins it.

o: the castor plant growing by the roadside
sandalwood, Ravidas's picture for the Lord
a silk cloth, dyed white and yellow

games.q: inside the hymn — tap the pairs.

s: in the hymn, the castor turns into sandalwood
it stays a castor plant; the fragrance comes to dwell in it because it grows near.
Ravidas seeks the shelter of the company of holy ones
the refrain asks Madho for the shelter of that company.

games.q: you're a lowly castor plant and you want to carry the sandalwood's scent. what does Ravidas's hymn say works?
o: work hard to become a different tree.
hide where no one can smell you.
games.why: living close beside You, he sings, the lowly tree became lofty, because Your fragrance came to dwell in it.

practice: Bring to mind one person whose goodness you can almost smell: the kind one, the patient one, the one who leaves a room lighter than they found it.
Picture yourself standing beside them for a minute, not trying to be like them, only near, and let something of them settle on you. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: Chandan. Sandalwood, Ravidas's picture for the Lord: a weedy castor plant growing beside it comes away made fragrant, just by standing close.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: chandan, sandalwood, the Lord's fragrance in Ravidas's hymn.

carryVoice: Your line: made fragrant. It's where you stand, not where you started. That's day seven hundred seventy-six.
